explanations: Hydrogen is the lightest and most abundant element in the universe, and its name means water-former, after what Cavendish saw it make when burned.
Helium was first spotted as a yellow line in sunlight during the eclipse of 1868 and named after the Sun; it is the second lightest element.
Lithium is a soft, silvery-white alkali metal, the least dense of all metals, and most of what is produced goes into batteries.
Hydrogen, helium and lithium are the first three chemical elements, with atomic numbers 1, 2 and 3.

sources.excerpt: It is the lightest and most abundant chemical element in the universe, constituting about 75% of all normal matter.

Henry Cavendish, in 1766–1781, identified hydrogen gas as a distinct substance and discovered its property of producing water when burned: this is the origin of hydrogen's name, which means 'water-former'

Helium was first detected as an unknown, yellow spectral line signature in sunlight during a solar eclipse in 1868 by Georges Rayet, Captain C. T. Haig, Norman R. Pogson, and Lieutenant John Herschel, and was subsequently confirmed by French astronomer Jules Janssen.
It is the second-lightest and second-most abundant element in the observable universe, after hydrogen.
It is a soft, silvery-white alkali metal. Under standard conditions, it is the least dense metal and the least dense solid element.
Batteries alone consume more than three-quarters of lithium production.
It is a colorless, odorless, non-toxic, inert, monatomic gas and the first in the noble gas group in the periodic table.
